history.summary: The Keshav Dev (Keshavdeva) temple stands at Katra Keshav Dev within the Shri Krishna Janmasthan complex, the traditional birthplace of Krishna. Tradition credits the first shrine to Vajranabha, Krishna's great-grandson; sources describe rebuilds under Chandragupta Vikramaditya and in 1150, destructions by Mahmud of Ghazni and Aurangzeb (the ASI's 1920 notification records the Keshavadeva temple dismantled and the site used for the Shahi Eidgah mosque). The present Keshavdeva temple was built by Ramkrishna Dalmia from 29 June 1957 and inaugurated 6 September 1958, south of the mosque. FLAG: CSV town 'Mathura Cantonment' corrected to Mathura (the complex lies in Mathura city proper, Govind Nagar); CSV 'state' column held the town name, corrected to Uttar Pradesh.

town_description: Mathura is a holy city on the Yamuna river, revered as the birthplace of Krishna and the centre of the Braj region. It is the headquarters of Mathura district in Uttar Pradesh and, together with Vrindavan, is among Hinduism's most visited pilgrimage centres.

travel.railway: Mathura Junction, close to the temple complex
travel.road: Mathura city on Janmabhoomi Marg, near the railway station; well connected by road to Agra and Delhi
